thread:
anya: Quick flag housekeeping convo. Ops noticed periodic bill spikes tied to a handful of long-lived flags. Proposing a 'reaping' flow for truly abandoned flags.

rahul: Can you define 'abandoned'? We need something reproducible.

lena: Suggestion: no edits in 180d AND no telemetry hits in 120d. Also owner_team is null or owner last-active > 120d.

dave: Sounds reasonable. Two concerns: a) computing 'no telemetry hits in 120d' needs a time series scan; b) reaping must not break running experiments.

anya: Totally. Plan is 3-step: mark -> notify -> reap. Mark would annotate flags with a candidate_reap_ts and reason. Notify sends owner/team email and adds console banner. After 7d with no response, eligible for reap.

infra-bot: Note: log retention is 30d by default. Long-range detection requires retention bump or an indexed summary table.

rahul: We should avoid changing production flag objects during mark step to reduce write surface. Use flags_annotations table keyed by flag_id with fields: candidate_reap_ts, reason, detected_by. That keeps core flag immutable.

lena: API-wise we can extend GraphQL: Flag.annotations -> [Annotation]. Add a mutation to acknowledge_annotation so owners can opt-out. Keep the acknowledge audit entry in audit_log.

dave: Good call re opt-out. Also add a transfer_owner mutation so SRE can quickly reassign if the team is defunct.

anya: UX asks: console row-level CTA 'Acknowledge / Transfer / Reap in 7d'. Also a bulk filter to list candidate flags by team/org and reason.

rahul: On reaping implementation, prefer a soft-reap that toggles to archived state (no evaluation) but preserves config in backup storage for 30 days. If traffic regression observed, we can un-archive quickly.

lena: We need a shadow test before actual reap. Router can route a sample (1%) traffic through a path that treats the flag as if it were absent and compare outputs for 24h. If divergence > 0.05% by error-class we abort.

infra-bot: Shadow sampling adds ~0.5% CPU on p50 for router pod. Need capacity check if we do many flags concurrently.

dave: Limit concurrent shadow-evals to 5 per cluster. Queue rest. Expose queue depth in console.

anya: Telemetry needs fields on the annotation index: detected_at, last_seen_ts, owner_team_hint, dryrun_status, ack_by. Also a human-readable reason string: "no-edit-180d" or "no-usage-120d".

rahul: For detection we can run two modes: full-scan (requires retention) and sampled-scan using existing 30d retention + extrapolation heuristics. Flag scoring gives confidence score; only high-confidence candidates enter notify stage.

lena: Confidence calc: 1. time since last edit, 2. last_seen_age, 3. owner_activity_score. Weighted sum -> 0-100%. Threshold 85% to notify.

dave: Ops alerting: send daily digest to team leads when they have > 5 candidate flags or any candidate flagged as 'impact_unknown'.

anya: Security: reaping must require two-actor approval for flags that are global-scope or used by > 3 services. Add a console modal that shows a small dependency tree.

rahul: We also need migration story for existing archived boolean field some services already use. The annotation should be the canonical source; add a migration job to backfill where archive=true -> add annotation reason=migrated-archived and preserve original actor.

infra-bot: Ticket created for retention increase request #4620. ETA pending.

dave: Action items: @lena design GraphQL additions + sample query for annotations, @rahul sketch detector job + confidence algorithm, @anya console mockups and runbook skeleton, @infra-bot follow-up on retention ticket. I'll own limiting concurrency and shadow queueer.

ops-bot: runbook stub created: /runbooks/flag-reap.md (draft).

anya: Let's spike this week on detector prototype and a console mock. Sync Thursday sync to review spike output. :calendar:
